19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49	
50	- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
51	- 重点学：
52	  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
53	  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
54	  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
55	  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
56	- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
57	- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 二、Abstract 写作规范
62	
63	### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）
64	
65	Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
66	1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
67	2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
68	3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
69	4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献
70	
71	### 2.2 禁忌
72	
73	- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim

3	\section{Introduction}
4	
5	Multi-turn jailbreak attacks distribute adversarial intent across individually benign turns. Crescendo~\citep{russinovich2024crescendo}, Foot-in-the-Door~\citep{fitd2024}, and Deceptive Delight~\citep{deceptivedelight2024} all rely on persuasion as their core mechanism: \citet{zeng2024pap} catalogue 40 persuasion techniques across jailbreak families, and \citet{hagendorff2026reasoning} identify strategies in 97\% of successful attacks. Because individual attack turns occupy the same embedding region as benign text~\citep{bullwinkel2025repeng}, no single-turn filter can distinguish them from legitimate conversation.
6	
7	Existing defenses leave a critical gap. Production classifiers such as Llama Guard~\citep{inan2023llamaguard}, WildGuard~\citep{han2024wildguard}, and ShieldGemma~\citep{zeng2024shieldgemma} operate on individual turns and miss multi-turn manipulation; Llama Guard~3 detects only 1.8\% of multi-turn jailbreaks in our evaluation (Section~\ref{sec:decomposition}). Multi-turn defenses (DeepContext~\citep{deepcontext2026}, BIID~\citep{tong2025biid}, G-Guard~\citep{gguard2025}) model conversation-level structure but each evaluates on a single attack family. None answers the central question: \emph{what representation properties enable a detector to generalize across attack families it has never seen?}
8	
9	Pretrained language understanding does not suffice at base model scale: vanilla DeBERTa-v3~\citep{he2021deberta} with temporal aggregation (cf.\ DeepContext) drops from F1\,=\,1.000 in-distribution to 0.312 on OOD Deceptive Delight, and GPT-5.5 reaches only 0.191--0.449 F1 with 30--47\% unparseable responses (Appendix~\ref{sec:llm_judge}). The bottleneck is distributional: cross-attack generalization requires domain adaptation, not a better classifier.

2	\begin{abstract}
3	Detecting unseen multi-turn jailbreaks requires domain adaptation, but the form of adaptation matters.
4	Multi-turn jailbreak attacks spread adversarial intent across benign-seeming turns, and existing defenses fail to generalize across attack families: Llama Guard~3, a widely deployed turn-level safety classifier, detects only 1.8\% of multi-turn jailbreaks in our evaluation.
5	We isolate the factors behind cross-attack generalization on synthetic multi-turn data through controlled ablation: thirteen encoder configurations at three scales (125 to 355M parameters) decompose the contributions of domain exposure, classification supervision, label quality, and granularity on three out-of-distribution (OOD) attack families and two training compositions.
6	On single-source synthetic data, continued pretraining closes roughly 60 percentage points of the OOD gap without labels. This effectiveness is condition-dependent: on mixed-LLM training data, unsupervised pretraining collapses while classification-based adaptation remains the strongest variant (DD OOD F1\,=\,0.818 vs.\ 0.291 without adaptation).
7	Across three architectures (125--355M), the set of attacks requiring adaptation shrinks with scale, though architecture and pretraining differences prevent isolating scale as the sole factor.
8	Classification supervision is associated with substantially lower prediction variance on synthetic evaluations (observed across 3 seeds), with attack-complexity-dependent sensitivity to label correctness, but this benefit reverses on human-authored data.
9	These findings suggest classification DAPT provides robustness through optimization regularization, not semantic feature learning.
10	\end{abstract}

tool_args.old_string:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=2pt, topsep=4pt]
  \item \textbf{Systematic decomposition identifying the most robust adaptation and three supplementary negative results.} Controlled ablation across thirteen encoder configurations on synthetic multi-turn data shows classification-based DAPT is the most robust variant; unsupervised pretraining is effective on single-source data but collapses on mixed-LLM training. We report three supplementary findings that challenge common assumptions: scrambled labels perform comparably to correct labels on template-based attacks (TOST-confirmed on DD and FITD at $n$\,=\,10) but show moderate sensitivity on structurally complex attacks ($d$\,=\,0.44 on ActorAttack), temporal order is irrelevant ($\Delta < 1$\,pp), and label granularity does not affect detection.

  \item \textbf{Architecture- and scale-dependent observation on domain adaptation.} Three encoder scales (125M, 184M, 355M) suggest adaptation need shrinks with model size, though encoders differ in architecture; same-architecture scaling is needed to isolate scale. RoBERTa-large handles structurally complex attacks without adaptation (Section~\ref{sec:cross_encoder}).

  \item \textbf{Mechanistic interpretation: optimization regularization, not semantic learning.} Two null results and one conditional finding converge: frozen probing near-parity (AA gap 3.1\,pp), temporal modeling irrelevance ($|\Delta| < 1$\,pp), and attack-complexity-dependent label sensitivity ($d \approx 0$ on DD/FITD, $d$\,=\,0.44 on ActorAttack) are consistent with classification supervision providing robustness primarily through optimization regularization that stabilizes downstream training. This benefit is condition-dependent (variance reversal on human data) but classification DAPT remains strongest under mixed-LLM training (Section~\ref{sec:discussion}). Continued pretraining is 24.3$\times$ faster than LLM-as-judge (Appendix~\ref{app:efficiency}).
\end{itemize}
tool_args.new_string:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=2pt, topsep=4pt]
  \item \textbf{Two-axis generalization decomposition.} We identify two orthogonal generalization challenges in multi-turn jailbreak detection. Attack-side: controlled ablation across thirteen encoder configurations reveals classification DAPT as the most robust variant (vanilla F1\,=\,0.28--0.31 on OOD $\rightarrow$ 0.97--1.0); unsupervised pretraining collapses under mixed-LLM training. Benign-side: 10 target-domain benign conversations eliminate WildChat FPR from 68.1\% to 0\% (95\% CI upper 6.1\%) without detection degradation.

  \item \textbf{Condition-dependent adaptation effectiveness and constraining negative results.} MLM is effective on single-source data but collapses under mixed-LLM training; classification DAPT is robust across conditions. Three supplementary negative results constrain which properties matter: scrambled labels perform comparably to correct labels on template-based attacks (TOST-confirmed on DD and FITD at $n$\,=\,10, $d$\,=\,0.44 on structurally complex ActorAttack), temporal order is irrelevant ($\Delta < 1$\,pp), and label granularity does not affect detection.

  \item \textbf{Practical deployment recipe.} Continued pretraining is 24.3$\times$ faster than LLM-as-judge (Appendix~\ref{app:efficiency}), and 10-shot benign adaptation eliminates domain-specific false positives. No target-domain attack data is required for deployment.
\end{itemize}

tool_args.old_string:
\paragraph{Benign distribution as the remaining bottleneck.}
OOD F1 figures are upper bounds (benign is IID). On WildChat, 9-class FPR reaches 68.1\% (Appendix~\ref{app:wildchat_fpr}); cross-LLM error decomposition confirms collapse is driven by false positives on unfamiliar benign text. A benign adaptation curve (Appendix~\ref{app:benign_mixed}) shows FPR drops from 68.1\% to 0\% with as few as 10 conversations (95\% CI upper 6.1\%, $n$\,=\,49) while all OOD F1 remains $\geq$\,0.953, confirming benign mismatch as the primary bottleneck.
tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Two-axis generalization: attack-side vs.\ benign-side.}
OOD F1 figures throughout this paper reflect attack-side generalization under IID benign conditions: DAPT closes the attack-side gap (vanilla F1\,=\,0.28--0.31 $\rightarrow$ 0.97--1.0 on OOD families). The orthogonal challenge is benign-side distribution shift. On WildChat, 9-class FPR reaches 68.1\% (Appendix~\ref{app:wildchat_fpr}); cross-LLM error decomposition confirms collapse is driven by false positives on unfamiliar benign text, not detection failure. A benign adaptation curve (Appendix~\ref{app:benign_mixed}) shows FPR drops from 68.1\% to 0\% with as few as 10 conversations (95\% CI upper 6.1\%, $n$\,=\,49) while all OOD F1 remains $\geq$\,0.953: the two axes are orthogonal and independently addressable.

tool_args.old_string:
\section{Conclusion}

On synthetic multi-turn evaluations, classification-based DAPT is the most robust adaptation for base-size encoders, providing robustness through optimization regularization rather than semantic learning; unsupervised pretraining collapses under mixed-LLM training. Label sensitivity is attack-complexity-dependent (TOST-confirmed equivalence on DD/FITD at $n$\,=\,10; $d$\,=\,0.44 on ActorAttack); negative results on temporal order and domain specificity further constrain which properties matter; continued pretraining is 24.3$\times$ faster than LLM-as-judge (Appendix~\ref{app:efficiency}), offering a practical alternative given matched benign distributions (Appendix~\ref{app:wildchat_fpr}).
tool_args.new_string:
\section{Conclusion}

Controlled ablation across thirteen encoder configurations decomposes multi-turn jailbreak generalization into two orthogonal axes. On the attack side, classification-based DAPT is the most robust adaptation for base-size encoders, providing robustness through optimization regularization rather than semantic learning; unsupervised pretraining collapses under mixed-LLM training. On the benign side, 10 target-domain benign conversations eliminate distributional false positives (WildChat FPR 68.1\%\,$\rightarrow$\,0\%) without detection degradation. Label sensitivity is attack-complexity-dependent (TOST-confirmed equivalence on DD/FITD at $n$\,=\,10; $d$\,=\,0.44 on ActorAttack); negative results on temporal order and label granularity further constrain which properties matter. Combined with 24.3$\times$ speedup over LLM-as-judge (Appendix~\ref{app:efficiency}), the two-axis decomposition yields a practical deployment recipe that requires no target-domain attack data.
